correctness.rationale: The three angle families, limit, and stated extremal range survive unchanged. In the intrinsic sum-zero space the outward normals are negative projected incidence vectors; their scalar product is |A intersection B|-|A||B|/(m+1). The nested fan identifies the three exhaustive compatible-pair types, and short binomial sums give the announced counts. The signs give exactly binom(m,2) acute ridges and no right ridges. For uniform ridge count the non-hub–hub families have mass O(m(2/3)^m), and the two empty-bin exclusions each have probability (2/3)^m under independent leaf coloring. The gradient of the limiting exterior cosine in the fractions in the first and third bins is (9/8,9/8), so the middle-bin variance gives 9/32 for the cosine; the supplement-angle derivative 2/sqrt(3) gives 3/8 and center 2pi/3. The 1/m hub correction is negligible in the CLT. For the maximum, fixed s forces t=s+1; strict log-concavity balances j and m-j. The repaired comparison at j=2 alone exceeds the squared leaf–hub maximum by (m-3)(m+1)/(6m(m-1)) for m>=4. Counting the one or two balanced indices gives the stated binomials, and arccos at 1 gives the 2/sqrt(m) deficit. Independent finite corroboration for m=2..6 used the co-minimizer sets of every ordered coordinate weak order on the individual simplices. For c connected components of the co-minimizer graph the affine rank is m+1-c, since the spanning directions are differences of tied coordinate vectors. Deduplicated faces gave respectively 5,24,84,265,803 ridges, exactly two containing facets per ridge, the claimed signed squared cosines, and maximum multiplicities 4,12,12,50,60 (the first two have mixed-family ties). Replay with python3 /workspace/branches/9e78c583-d297-49c1-bd08-2c06eecfe717/enumerate_stellohedron.py; full signed-square counts are in enumeration_results.txt in that directory. The analytic proof covers all dimensions and the asymptotic limit; the finite check does not. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.

evidence: For a flag A subset B, the corresponding braid blocks are (A,B\A,V\B). At fixed sizes (a,b,c) the braid multiplicity is N!/(a!b!c!). Hub–hub restricts to hub in block one, giving weight factor a/N; leaf–hub requires first block singleton and hub in block two, giving factor b/N on those triples. Disjoint leaves are not a flag and provide a separate atom.

The same-date braid result explicitly gives the identical nested cosine and Gaussian center/variance. Forcing a label into block one perturbs normalized counts by O(1/m), so the star's bulk consequence follows from the same CLT. Its unrestricted angle formula also has the same maximum value (middle block singleton and the remaining sizes balanced); the star's distinct maximizing counts require the hub restrictions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is genuine overlapping mathematics, not just similar wording. The angle function, leading Gaussian law and maximal value are not independent evidence of originality. The full star spectrum is neither the complete unconditioned braid law nor the standard parking law: to obtain it one must classify the allowable normal pairs, reweight both nested classes and add the nonflag acute contribution, with a separate check that mixed ridges do not supply additional extreme counts for m>=4.

value.rationale: The quantity is a natural exact metric invariant of the canonical stellohedron, not a new name for an f-vector or a generic inner-product formula. The class weights resolve precisely the change in ridge geometry hidden by an unchanged combinatorial type: the standard-coordinate parking realization has right angles and no acute ones in the stellohedral regime, while this intrinsic realization has no right angles and an exact acute population. Despite sharing the braid bulk limit and maximal angle value, its exact rare-angle frequencies and parity-dependent maximizing population differ. A researcher comparing stellohedral realizations or computing exact unweighted angle statistics needs the full census, not the individual nested angle or its CLT alone.
